To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we present a novel algorithm for the detection of social groups in crowds; (ii) the algorithm learns the affinity among people through a set of features characterizing both the social and the physical identity of individuals; (iii) we show that our approach achieves state-of-the art performances in the challenging task of social groups detection in crowds.

we propose a novel method to learn social constraints from data and use them to detect groups in crowds; we propose a novel loss function to evaluate group detection performances; we show the effectiveness of our algorithm on real-world datasets.

we propose a novel approach for group detection in crowds, that we introduce a novel loss function to evaluate group detection performances, and that we achieve state-of-the-art performances when relying on both real trajectories and tracklets extracted by state-of-the-art detectors/tracker systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. What are the best features to characterize the interactions among people in a crowd? How to combine these features to learn the affinity matrix? How can we evaluate group detection performance in crowds?
the development of novel algorithms for crowd understanding, which are able to capture the underlying social structure and dynamics.

the following aspects: (1) the definition of new features for the analysis of social groups in crowds; (2) the design of a novel algorithm to detect social groups; (3) the definition of an evaluation protocol to measure the performance of group detection algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to detect social groups of people in crowded scenes by exploiting both physical and social features.
our approach is a promising tool for social group detection in crowds.

we have proposed and evaluated an algorithm for detecting social group in crowds by means a Correlation Clusters procedure on people trajectories, where the affinity between crowd members has been learned through an online formualtion of the Structural SVM framewok and a set of specific designed features characterizing the physical and social identity inspired by Proxemics theory, Granger Causality, DTW, and Heat-maps, and where the loss function is able to deal with complex evaluation of group detection performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach to the problem of detecting groups in crowds.
, by learning a set of social constraints on crowd members' trajectories, we achieve state-of-the-art group detection results on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
we propose a novel framework to detect social groups in crowd scenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

social groups can be detected from raw video streams, without the need for complex tracking systems, and that the social structure of crowds can be inferred by means of simple, interpretable and efficient learning algorithms.
, even in a crowd, the social structure is still visible and can be exploited to improve group detection.

, even if the detection of social groups is still an open problem, it is possible to achieve a good performance by means of a simple and efficient algorithm that can be easily implemented and integrated into existing crowd analysis systems.
